newsitem.title: USA: Task force endorses use of utility accounting rule.
newsitem.headline: Task force endorses use of utility accounting rule.

text.p: A task force convened by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) tentatively agreed Thursday that utilities can continue to use special accounting standards for generation assets while the industry undergoes deregulation, a FASB staff member said.

The task force members approved the idea of utilities continuing to use Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (SFAS) No. 71 during a transition period, as long as regulators ensure recovery of the assets by means of non-bypassable charges on all customers bills.

SFAS No. 71 allows utilities to record certain regulatory assets and liabilities which would be included in future rates and would not be recorded under generally accepted accounting principles for nonregulated entitites.

Given efforts by several states, including California, to end regulated electric utility monopolies and introduce retail market competition, continued use of the accounting standard was brought into question.

At Thursday's meeting, the task force tentatively decided that the accumulated balances of regulated entities under SFAS No. 71 can be separated under deregulation and assigned to the regulated business segment under which they will be recovered in the future, said FASB staff member Julie Erhardt.

Utilities such as California-based PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co have warned that continued application of the accounting standard was crucial to a smooth transition toward a competitive electricity industry.

If the FASB, or the Securities and Exchange Commission, were to conclude that California's regulatory and legal framework no longer met the requirements to apply SFAS No. 71 to generation assets, PG&E would have to take a material write-off, the utility said in its annual report.
As a result of applying the provision, PG&E said it had accumulated around $1.6 billion of regulatory assets attributable to electric generation as of the end of 1996.
The FASB-sponsored task force will meet again on July 24.
